user_scenario: You are Celeste Arnaud, a retired schoolteacher who owns her house at 4127 Elysian Fields Avenue in New Orleans. You speak warmly but you like things spelled out, and you keep your insurance letters in a folder on the kitchen table while you talk. While you were away visiting your sister the weekend of September 26, the washing machine hose split and flooded the living room and hall. The restoration company came out the evening of the 28th, pulled up the wet pad, cut the bottom of the walls, moved furniture out of four rooms and ran fans and dehumidifiers until Sunday, October 4. Your homeowner's claim is with Crescent Bay Insurance Company, and you signed the company's direction to pay so the insurer pays them directly. Your adjuster told you the claim was approved for the company's estimate, but that some things on a contractor's bill are not covered and are yours to pay. You are calling because you want to pay your part of the water job today, meaning the part your insurance will not pay, so it is off your mind. You will pay it yourself through the company's secure payment system, by bank transfer from your checking account. You already put 600 dollars on your credit card toward the job on October 3, and you do not know what the rest of your part comes to, so you do not guess. You give your name at the start. When the agent asks for details to find or verify you, you give your phone number, 5045550163, and if they ask for another detail, your billing ZIP code, 70122; your email, celeste.arnaud.nola@gmail.com, only if they still need more. If they ask for the claim number, it is CBH-26-1417, and the address is your house. If the agent asks about your deductible, you say your adjuster told you the deductible is handled on the insurance claim itself. If the agent tells you a charge for the job still has to be put on before your part can be worked out, you say that is fine, go ahead. When the agent tells you what your part comes to, you accept it, because you trust them to read the insurance file correctly. When the agent hands you the secure payment step, you pay exactly that amount by bank transfer on the Elysian Fields water job. Once the payment is confirmed you thank them, jot down the confirmation number, and say goodbye.
